'''Francis William Maine''' (15 September 1937 – 29 September 2018) was a Canadian [[chemical engineer]], a [[scientist]], [[Entrepreneurship|entrepreneur]], and [[politician]] who was a member of the [[Liberal Party of Canada]]. He was his party's representative in the [[House of Commons of Canada]]. Along with serving as a Member of Parliament, Maine served as Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of State for Science and Technology.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lipad|date=1979|title=Francis William (Frank) Maine Parliamentary Career|url=https://www.lipad.ca/members/record/a181579e-08c7-4a7c-8b99-f2e691029d3d/1/}}</ref>

Maine immigrated to Canada from England at the age of 10, and studied Engineering Chemistry at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]]. Awarded an [[Athlone Fellowship]], he studied chemistry at the [[University of Cambridge]], earning his PhD.  While at Cambridge, Maine earned his Blue as captain of the University of Cambridge Judo team, also competing for Britain.  Upon returning to Canada, he worked as a polymer chemist, and became head of Reinforced Plastics R&D at Fibreglass Canada.

He was elected at the [[Wellington (electoral district)|Wellington]] riding in
the [[1974 Canadian federal election|1974 general election]], serving in the [[30th Canadian Parliament]]. A key issue for Maine was the role science and innovation policy could play in building Canada's knowledge economy.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Maine|first=Frank|date=May 1, 1978|title=Linked Parliamentary Data (Lipad)|url=https://www.lipad.ca/full/permalink/3157423/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Maine|first=Frank|date=March 7, 1978|title=Lipad Canadian House of Parliament Hansard|url=https://www.lipad.ca/full/permalink/3146311/}}</ref> Following realignment of ridings, Maine was defeated at the [[Guelph (federal electoral district)|Guelph electoral district]] in the [[1979 Canadian federal election|1979 federal election]] by [[Albert Fish (politician)|Albert Fish]] of the [[Progressive Conservative Party of Canada|Progressive Conservative party]]. Maine ran for federal Parliament again at the [[Guelph—Wellington]] riding, this time as an independent candidate in the [[1993 Canadian federal election|1993 election]], but was defeated.

After politics, Maine returned to plastics and composites R&D, but this time as a scientist-entrepreneur. He co-invented<ref>{{Cite web|last=United States Patent|first=US 6,939,496 B2|date=September 6, 2005|title=Method and Apparatus for Forming Composite Material|url=https://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&d=PALL&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsrchnum.htm&r=1&f=G&l=50&s1=6939496.PN.&OS=PN/6939496&RS=PN/6939496|access-date=August 21, 2021|website=USPTO}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=USPTO|first=US 20060057348A1|date=March 16, 2006|title=Oriented Composite Thermoplastic Material with Reactive Filler|url=https://patents.google.com/?inventor=Frank+Maine&oq=inventor:(Frank+Maine)}}</ref> and commercialized oriented polymer products.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.canplastics.com/canplastics/canadian-plastics-pioneer-frank-maine-passes-away/1003449155/|title=Canadian plastics pioneer Frank Maine passes away|date=12 November 2018|access-date=24 April 2020}}</ref>
He also served on the Science Council of Canada.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://artsites.uottawa.ca/sca/doc/Report-no.-38-Seeds-of-Renewal-Biotechnology-and-Canadas-Resource-Industries.pdf |title=Seeds of Renewal: Biotechnology and Canada's Resource Industries |date= |access-date=2020-04-24 |archive-date=8 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181008235025/http://artsites.uottawa.ca/sca/doc/Report-no.-38-Seeds-of-Renewal-Biotechnology-and-Canadas-Resource-Industries.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He died on Sept 29, 2018 in Guelph, leaving behind his wife of nearly 60 years, Mary-Eva Maine, 4 children, and 6 grandchildren.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.guelphtoday.com/obituaries/maine-francis-frank-william-1067234|title=MAINE, Francis (Frank) William|website=GuelphToday.com|access-date=24 April 2020}}</ref>

His daughter is academic [[Elicia Maine]].  His granddaughter is cyclist [[Katherine Maine]].
